summary: WP-002 passes code review. Implementation in gui/api.ts is clean, consistent with existing handler patterns, and correctly separated from the storage-layer logic already reviewed in WP-001.
RenameBodySchema is correctly hoisted to module scope and exported; the .refine() constraint enforces the at-least-one-field invariant at parse time so no runtime null-guard is needed elsewhere.

SAFE_SLUG_REGEX early-reject guard in handleRenameProject is sound defence-in-depth: same constraints as the storage layer, but surfaces a typed VALIDATION_ERROR rather than a raw thrown Error.
Operation ordering (title first, slug second) is correct; latestMeta! non-null assertion is safe and the comment makes the reasoning explicit.

QA bug fix (missing CONFLICT wrapping around renameSlug()) was necessary and well-executed; the targeted catch block correctly distinguishes conflict errors from unexpected I/O errors and re-throws anything else.

One edge case worth tracking: when the caller sends { slug: currentSlug } (same-slug no-op), renameSlug() throws Error('Slug is already "…"') but the catch block does not handle that prefix, so it propagates as an unhandled 500. Low-severity (unusual usage) but not intentionally handled.
JSDoc is comprehensive and accurate — documents all error codes, the last_updated invariant, and the store-reuse warning.
api-surface.md updated correctly with new schema signature, CONFLICT error code, and operation-order note.

All 7 new QA tests are well-structured: isolate correctly by unique slug prefixes, cover disk side-effects, last_updated invariant, combined request, invalid slug regex, and CONFLICT. Full suite 1100 tests pass.

comments.note: Same-slug no-op is an unhandled 500. In handleRenameProject (gui/api.ts), when the caller sends { slug: currentSlug }, store.renameSlug() throws Error('Slug is already "…"; no rename needed.'). The catch block only matches the 'Slug already in use:' prefix and re-throws everything else, so this escapes as an unhandled error. Options: (a) catch this prefix and return the current meta as a no-op 200; (b) catch it as a VALIDATION_ERROR 400; (c) add a pre-check before calling renameSlug() (compare newSlug === slug). Option (a) is the most user-friendly. Not blocking but worth addressing in a follow-up.

The CONFLICT catch block in handleRenameProject uses string-prefix matching (msg.startsWith('Slug already in use:')) to detect the renameSlug() conflict sentinel. This is tight coupling to an internal error message format. A lightweight alternative would be a typed SlugConflictError class in ledger-store.ts so the catch can use instanceof — eliminates string coupling without significant refactor. Non-blocking given both files are internal.

No test covers the same-slug no-op path (PATCH /projects/:slug with { slug: currentSlug }). Given the 500-path issue noted above, adding a test for this would both document the intended behaviour and drive the fix. Recommend adding to api.test.ts handleRenameProject describe block.
